title: White Label GEO Services and Local SEO for Agencies
excerpt: What white label GEO services deliver, what changes on a client's website, how to price and resell them under your brand, and why GEO belongs with local SEO.
content:
Yes. asparagents offers GEO (AI visibility) and local SEO as a white label service, delivered under your agency's brand next to SEO, social media management and monthly reports. You keep the client relationship and the invoice; we do the work in the background and hand you reports you can send as your own. That lets a small web studio or social agency sell AI visibility without hiring a specialist.

It matters because more answers now sit on the results page itself. In a Pew Research Center study of 900 US adults' browsing in March 2025, people clicked a traditional search result on 8% of visits to Google pages with an AI summary, against 15% on pages without one, and clicked a link inside the summary on 1% of visits. When fewer people click through, being named in the answer counts for more.

This guide explains what GEO is, what a white label GEO service should deliver each month, why it belongs next to local SEO, and how onboarding works.

What is GEO and how does it differ from SEO?

GEO stands for generative engine optimization. It is the work of making a business show up, and be described correctly, in the answers that AI assistants give, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google's AI Overviews.

SEO aims for a place in the list of search results. GEO aims for a mention inside the answer itself. The two overlap more than the new name suggests. Google says the same SEO best practices apply to its AI features, that there are no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode, and that no new machine readable files or special structured data are needed. In practice, GEO builds on SEO and adds three things:

  • Prompt tracking. Checking, every month, which businesses the assistants recommend for the questions your client's buyers actually ask.
  • Answer ready content. Pages that answer those questions directly, with clear facts about services, location and prices where the client publishes them.
  • Consistent facts across the web. The same name, address, phone, services and description on the website, the Google Business Profile and the directories the assistants read.

The research that gave GEO its name points the same way. In a 2024 paper presented at KDD, the authors tested ways of rewriting web content and found that adding quotations, statistics and cited sources made a page markedly more visible in AI generated answers, by up to about 40% on their main measure, while keyword stuffing made it slightly worse than doing nothing.

What does a white label GEO service deliver each month?

Whoever you partner with, ask for a written list of monthly deliverables. A useful service covers at least:

  • A prompt list per client. The buyer questions to track, agreed with you at the start.
  • Monthly AI visibility checks. Whether the client is named or cited for each prompt, which competitors appear instead, and which sources the assistants used.
  • Fixes on the website. Service pages, FAQs and structured data that make the client's facts easy to quote.
  • Local SEO work. Google Business Profile updates, posts, categories and a review strategy.
  • A report you can forward. Plain language, no jargon, in your agency's name.

What changes on the client's website?

Most GEO fixes are ordinary website work, done with the answer in mind:

  • Let the assistants in. ChatGPT search finds pages through OpenAI's OAI-SearchBot crawler, and OpenAI says sites that opt out of it will not appear in ChatGPT search answers. Its other crawler, GPTBot, only decides whether content may be used to train OpenAI's models, so a client can block training and still be found.
  • Answer the buyer's question first. A short, direct answer at the top of the page, then the detail.
  • Give facts worth quoting. Services, service areas, prices where the client publishes them, figures and named sources: the kind of content the GEO research found assistants pick up.
  • Keep structured data honest. Google says there is no special schema for its AI features and that structured data should match the visible text on the page.

Why pair GEO with local SEO and the Google Business Profile?

Most small business clients sell in one city or region. When a buyer asks an assistant for "a good accountant near me" or "the best dentist in Leeds", the answer leans on the same signals that drive Google's local results. Google says local results are based mainly on relevance, distance and prominence, that businesses with complete and accurate information are more likely to show up, and that there is no way to pay for a better local ranking.

That is why we treat GEO and local SEO as one service. A profile with the right categories, a clear description, recent photos and steady reviews helps the client in the map pack, and it gives the assistants consistent facts to repeat. Selling them separately usually means one half is done well and the other is not done at all.

How does the agency show results to its client?

GEO is new to most small business owners, so the report has to do some explaining. A good monthly report answers four questions:

  • Were we mentioned? For each tracked prompt and engine, named, cited or absent, compared with last month.
  • Who was mentioned instead? The competitors and the sources the answers relied on.
  • What did we change? The fixes made this month on the site and the profile.
  • What happens next? The plan for the coming month.

Next to that sit the usual numbers: Search Console clicks and impressions, Business Profile calls and direction requests, and leads where tracking allows. AI answers vary from one run to the next, so we report trends over several months rather than promising a fixed position.

What do onboarding and month one look like?

  1. Intro call. You tell us about the client, their market and what they sell. We agree the prompt list and the report format.
  2. Access. We work with access to the website, Search Console, Google Analytics and the Business Profile, granted through your agency's accounts.
  3. Baseline audit. A first AI visibility check and a local SEO review, so there is a clear starting point.
  4. First fixes. The quick wins from the audit: profile gaps, missing service pages, inconsistent facts.
  5. First report. At the end of month one, in your brand, ready to forward.

We never contact your client directly unless you ask us to.

How do agencies price and resell white label GEO?

With asparagents you set the price for your client, sell the service under your own brand, pay us a wholesale fee and keep the margin. Before any work starts you get a written list of what we deliver each month and the price, so you can build your own package around it.

There are two simple ways to package it: as an add-on to an SEO or website care plan you already sell, or as a separate AI visibility package with its own monthly report. Selling it together with local SEO is easier to explain to a small business owner, because one report covers both the map pack and the AI answers. See how our white label partnership works.

How do you choose a white label GEO partner?

  • Ask to see a sample report before you sign.
  • Ask which AI engines are checked and how often.
  • Ask what is done on the site each month, not only what is measured.
  • Make sure local SEO is included, or priced clearly beside it.
  • Check that all accounts stay in your agency's or your client's name.
  • Be wary of anyone who guarantees a mention in a specific AI answer.

FAQ

Is GEO a replacement for SEO?

No. GEO builds on SEO. A site that search engines cannot crawl or understand is unlikely to be quoted by an AI assistant either.

Can you guarantee my client appears in ChatGPT?

No one can. AI answers change between runs and between users. What we can do is track the prompts, fix what holds the client back and show the trend every month.

Will my client know you are involved?

Only if you want them to. Reports go out in your agency's name and we do not contact the client directly unless you ask.

Do you work with agencies outside the UK and US?

Yes. We already work behind the scenes for partner agencies in the UK, the US, mainland Europe and South Africa, and we work worldwide in English or Turkish.
